Disease Outbreak Disrupts Oil & Gas Operations in Curacao

A sudden outbreak of leptospirosis has struck workers at oil and gas production sites in Curacao, causing significant operational disruptions across the island’s energy sector. BB Energy Holdings NV and several other producers have reported staff shortages and temporary site closures as local health authorities work to contain the situation.

The outbreak, first identified late last week, has now affected over 60 employees at various terminals and offshore facilities, according to a statement from the Curacao Oil & Gas Producers Association (COGPA). Leptospirosis, a bacterial infection often spread through contaminated water, poses particular challenges given Curacao’s humid climate and the proximity of many sites to coastal marshlands.

“Operations at our Bullenbaai terminal are currently reduced to essential staff only,” a spokesperson for BB Energy Holdings NV confirmed. “We are prioritising the health and safety of our workforce while working closely with medical teams and local authorities.”

Production volumes across the island have dropped by an estimated 18% since the outbreak began, according to COGPA. Tanker scheduling at several ports has been delayed, and maintenance activities at some facilities have been suspended indefinitely. COGPA’s interim chair, Willem Martina, stated, “Our members are facing unprecedented disruptions. Sick leave has risen sharply, and we are coordinating with health officials to implement screening and sanitation measures.”

Worker representatives have raised concerns about site hygiene and protective protocols. “We’re urging all companies to review their water management and sanitation procedures,” said Jorge Peralta, regional leader of the Oilfield Workers Union. “Our members’ health must come first.”

Local analysts warn that continued disruption could impact exports if containment measures are not effective within the next two weeks. The situation remains fluid, with health teams conducting daily screenings and companies preparing for further operational adjustments. As of today, no timeline has been given for a full resumption of normal activities at affected sites.
